(2025), and the Computerized Sales and Inventory System with Stock Monitoring and Income Reporting for MacSull Grocery developed by Illustrisimo et al. (2026). Each system addresses a specific aspect of organizational management, including electronic voting, event coordination, online pre-ordering, financial management, and inventory monitoring. Collectively, these systems demonstrate how digital technologies improve operational efficiency, transparency, and service delivery within their respective domains. However, Hiusa distinguishes itself by integrating these organizational functions into a single AI-assisted student governance platform specifically designed for student body organizations.

While the Student Government E-Voting Application focuses primarily on conducting secure electronic elections, the UTHM Campus Event Management System specializes in organizing campus activities, and the KDK College Canteen Ordering Portal streamlines tokenized online ordering and product distribution. Similarly, the Computerized Sales and Inventory System emphasizes inventory monitoring, sales processing, and financial reporting for retail operations. In contrast, Hiusa consolidates these capabilities into a unified platform by integrating Electronic Voting Systems, Event Management Systems, Online Pre-Ordering Systems, Financial Information Systems, Inventory Management Systems, Biometric Identification Systems, Workflow Automation Systems, and Decision Support Systems. This comprehensive integration enables student organizations to manage governance, finances, organizational activities, and resource administration through a centralized web-based platform.  
&nbsp;Furthermore, Hiusa incorporates multiple AI-assisted technologies that extend beyond the capabilities of the systems reviewed. These include an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression model for financial forecasting, a Budget Advisory System for spending recommendations, a Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm for intelligent officer task delegation, and a Large Language Model (LLM) accessed through the Groq API. The LLM supports announcement drafting, AI-assisted event planning, and the automatic generation of human-readable financial reports, including income statements, expense summaries, audit logs, and event-specific financial reports based on recorded organizational transactions and OLS-generated forecasts. The reports can be exported in PDF and Excel formats, enabling student leaders to efficiently document, review, and present financial information while supporting evidence-based organizational decision-making.&nbsp;  
&nbsp;In addition, Hiusa provides four distinct user roles: Students, SBO Officers, Administrators, and Department Heads. Students can participate in electronic voting, reserve organizational merchandise, receive announcements and event notifications, and verify event attendance through the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader. Officers are assigned operational responsibilities such as completing delegated tasks, monitoring assigned activities, and participating in organizational workflows without full administrative privileges. Administrators, including the Student Body Organization (SBO) President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer or Auditor, Adviser, and, when applicable, the SBO Developer, manage organizational finances, events, inventories, elections, announcements, workflows, user accounts, and AI-assisted decision-support tools while performing administrative approvals and maintaining organizational records. Department Heads oversee organizational performance by reviewing reports, monitoring governance activities, and, when required, approving administrative actions, thereby providing an additional layer of institutional oversight and accountability.  
&nbsp;In conclusion, the comparative analysis demonstrates that although the reviewed systems effectively address individual organizational functions such as elections, event coordination, merchandise ordering, financial management, or inventory monitoring, none integrates these capabilities into a single intelligent governance platform

# **CHAPTER III**

# **DESIGN AND METHODOLOGY**

This chapter outlines the research and development methodologies implemented in Hiusa: an AI-integrated student governance and financial management system for Student Body Organizations at the University of Cebu – Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue. It discusses the research design, target respondents, research instruments, data-gathering procedures, and statistical treatments used to evaluate the proposed system's effectiveness. The researchers also present the software engineering methodology guiding the system's development in this chapter, with a comprehensive description of each phase: planning, analysis, design, development, testing, and evaluation. Furthermore, this chapter presents the ethical considerations, proposed system architecture, AI-driven functionalities, and development protocols to ensure the systematic implementation, reliability, and validity of the proposed system.

## **Research Design**

The research design serves as the overall plan and framework guiding the conduct of a research study. It outlines a blueprint for addressing the research questions, including processes for data collection, analysis, and interpretation. A well-structured research design ensures the study is conducted methodically and produces valid results (Taherdoost, 2022). To promote objective analysis and evidence-based decision-making, quantitative research focuses on collecting numerical data and applying statistical techniques.

Consequently, to achieve the stated objectives and support the development of the proposed system, this quantitative study will use a descriptive–quantitative research design. The descriptive component will identify and evaluate existing procedures, operational challenges, and organizational requirements associated with student governance, financial management, event planning, merchandise operations, attendance monitoring, and election management. Studies that seek to characterize current situations and produce quantifiable conclusions without changing variables are suitable for descriptive quantitative research (Taherdoost, 2022). By employing this design, the researchers hope to identify organizational needs, find gaps, and lay the foundation for the proposed system.

In the context of this study and its relevance to the selected research design, the study will use structured survey questionnaires distributed within the Student Body Organizations (SBO) of the University of Cebu – Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue, targeting a maximum total of 450 respondents composed of current and former SBO officers, SBO advisers, and students. The researchers will design the survey to gather quantitative data regarding existing organizational practices, governance operations, financial processes, event management activities, merchandise operations, attendance procedures, election methods, user requirements, and system expectations. The survey will also identify existing challenges and operational gaps within the participating organizations and collect user feedback to guide the design and refinement of the proposed system's features. Additionally, the collected responses will offer quantifiable data needed to verify the features and overall direction of the proposed system. Researchers recognize structured surveys as effective instruments for obtaining standardized and quantifiable information that supports reliable analysis and interpretation (Taherdoost, 2022).

Additionally, the researchers will use descriptive statistics such as frequencies, percentages, and weighted means to analyze the responses after data collection. Frequency and percentage will summarize respondent profiles and determine the distribution of responses across measured variables. Meanwhile, the weighted mean will be employed to determine the overall assessment and level of acceptability of the proposed system based on respondents' evaluations. These statistical treatments will provide measurable and organized interpretations of the collected data and support the identification of operational requirements and user perceptions relevant to the development and refinement of Hiusa. The findings from the statistical analysis will serve as the basis for validating system functionality, refining the proposed features of Hiusa, and ensuring alignment with organizational needs and user expectations (Taherdoost, 2022).&nbsp;

Given the nature of the capstone project, the overall methodology likewise incorporates elements of developmental research. Developmental research emphasizes the systematic design, development, implementation, and evaluation of systems to ensure that the final product remains functional and responsive to user requirements (Taherdoost, 2022). The developmental component will guide the creation and continuous refinement of Hiusa, including its AI-driven financial forecasting, budget advisory, workflow automation, event and activity management, attendance tracking, merchandise operations, and secure digital voting functionalities.

To support the developmental component, the study will employ the Agile Software Engineering Methodology, which emphasizes iterative development, continuous feedback, flexibility, and progressive enhancement throughout the system life cycle. Agile enables incremental implementation and refinement of system components while allowing modifications in response to stakeholder feedback and evolving requirements (Ghimire & Charters, 2022).

Finally, the combined use of descriptive–quantitative and developmental research design, specifically the Agile Software Engineering Methodology, ensures that the study produces reliable and measurable results while also supporting Hiusa's systematic design, development, evaluation, and ongoing improvement, guaranteeing that the proposed system is evidence-based and meets the operational demands and expectations of its intended environment.

**Method.** Following the adopted research design, the researchers will administer the validated survey questionnaire to the selected respondents after securing the necessary approvals from the concerned offices and participants. The researchers will collect the completed questionnaires and organize the responses through coding and tabulation to prepare the data for statistical analysis.

After data collection, the researchers will analyze the responses using descriptive statistics, specifically frequencies, percentages, and weighted means. These statistical techniques will summarize the respondent profiles, determine the distribution of responses, evaluate the identified organizational requirements, and assess the acceptability of the proposed system. Using the analysis findings, the researchers will determine the system requirements and validate Hiusa's proposed features.

The researchers will then use the findings from the analysis throughout the development of Hiusa, following the Agile Software Engineering Methodology. The system will undergo iterative phases of planning, design, development, testing, evaluation, and refinement based on stakeholder feedback. This approach will support the continuous improvement of the proposed system and ensure that it meets the operational requirements of the Student Body Organizations at the University of Cebu–Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue.

**Flow of the Study.** The diagram below (Figure 6\) illustrates the research process. It begins with identifying gaps and challenges in the existing student governance, financial management, event coordination, merchandise operations, and election processes of the Student Body Organizations (SBOs) at the University of Cebu–Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue. The study then determines the system requirements, defines the essential functionalities of the proposed system, and assesses its acceptability. After collecting sufficient data through survey questionnaires, the researchers proceed to system development, applying the adopted research design and the Agile Software Engineering Methodology. These processes lead to the development of Hiusa: An AI-Integrated Student Governance and Financial Management System, which aims to improve transparency, operational efficiency, decision-making, and overall student governance management through AI-driven financial forecasting, workflow automation, event management, merchandise coordination, attendance monitoring, and secure digital voting.&nbsp;

The collected responses will help the researchers identify operational requirements, validate system functionality, and support the development, testing, and refinement of Hiusa’s AI-assisted features, including financial forecasting, budget advisory, workflow automation, attendance monitoring, merchandise management, and digital election capabilities.

&nbsp;Overall, the study seeks to include students, SBO officers, and SBO advisers who serve as the primary stakeholders and intended users of the proposed system. Their collective perspectives will be essential in evaluating existing organizational practices, identifying operational requirements, and determining whether Hiusa effectively addresses the governance, financial management, and administrative needs of Student Body Organizations at the University of Cebu–Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue.

**Research Instrument.**	To achieve the objectives of this study, the researchers will use three structured survey questionnaires as the primary research instruments—one for students, one for Student Body Organization officers, and one for organization advisers at the University of Cebu – Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue (UCLM). Although the questionnaires will follow a shared five-section structure, their contents will vary according to each respondent group's roles, responsibilities, and experiences in Student Body Organization operations.  
&nbsp;Section A will collect demographic and organizational information while maintaining respondents' confidentiality. Section B will identify the current processes used in financial management, event coordination, task delegation, attendance monitoring, elections, merchandise distribution, communication, and organizational oversight. Section C will use Likert-scale items to determine existing problems, operational difficulties, and the perceived need for a centralized system. Section D will evaluate the proposed features of Hiusa, including AI-assisted financial management, event and task management, attendance tracking, secure digital elections, merchandise management, announcements, notifications, and organizational oversight. Student items will focus on accessibility, participation, usability, elections, merchandise, and communication. Officer items will focus on operational efficiency, financial management, coordination, and administration, while adviser items will focus on monitoring, accountability, transparency, and oversight. Section E will assess the overall acceptability of Hiusa and include open-ended questions for recommendations and additional feedback.  
&nbsp;Before administration, qualified experts will validate the questionnaires to ensure that the items are clear, relevant, appropriate, and aligned with the study objectives. The researchers will revise the instruments based on the validators' comments and recommendations before distributing them to the actual respondents.  
&nbsp;The researchers will also use authorized organizational records and operational documents as secondary research instruments. These may include financial records, event documents, election procedures, attendance records, merchandise processes, and organizational workflows. The researchers will check the documents for authenticity, relevance, completeness, and consistency and use them to validate the system requirements and guide the development of Hiusa.

**Research Procedure.** The researchers will follow a systematic procedure to collect, process, and analyze data to identify existing practices, operational challenges, and system requirements related to student governance, financial management, event coordination, merchandise operations, attendance monitoring, and election processes.

Initially, the researchers will obtain the required permissions from the University of Cebu—Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue (UCLM) by submitting a transmittal letter and required documents to the appropriate authorities. After receiving approval, the researchers will distribute printed survey questionnaires to selected respondents, including students, Student Body Organization officers, and advisers.

Next, the researchers will collect the completed questionnaires and check them for completeness and accuracy. The researchers will then consolidate, organize, and analyze the collected data to identify current practices, operational issues, and user requirements. Finally, the researchers will use the findings to evaluate and refine the proposed Hiusa system.

### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;**Data Gathering Procedure.** The researchers will conduct data collection in several stages. First, the researchers will prepare and validate the structured survey questionnaires to ensure alignment with the study's objectives. To obtain permission to conduct the study and distribute the questionnaires, the researchers will send a transmittal letter to the relevant university authorities. After receiving approval, the researchers will personally distribute printed copies of the survey questionnaires to the selected respondents. The researchers will allow sufficient time for the respondents to complete the questionnaires and will provide clarification when necessary. The researchers will collect the accomplished questionnaires and review all responses to ensure completeness. The researchers will then encode the responses into a digital format for organization and analysis. This process ensures accurate and complete data collection to support requirement validation and system development.

### &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;**Statistical Treatment of Data.** After collecting all responses, the researchers will organize, tabulate, and analyze the data to interpret the findings and support system evaluation. The researchers will use the following statistical tools:

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;***Frequency and Percentag*e.** The researchers will use frequencies and percentages to summarize the respondents' demographic profiles and identify patterns in current practices in student governance, financial management, event coordination, merchandise operations, attendance monitoring, and election processes. These measures will also help identify common issues, system requirements, and user expectations.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;***Weighted Mean*.** The researchers will use the weighted mean to compute the average responses based on the Likert-scale items. The researchers will determine the respondents' degree of agreement with the identified issues and system requirements, as well as the Hiusa system's acceptability in terms of functionality, usability, efficiency, and relevance.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;***Scoring Procedure*.** The researchers will use a five-point Likert scale to gauge respondents' levels of agreement or disagreement with each statement. This approach will allow the researchers to analyze respondents' perceptions, evaluate system features, and determine the overall acceptability of the proposed system.

&nbsp;**Ethical Considerations.** Before data collection, the researchers secured the institutional clearances required by the University of Cebu – Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue (UCLM). The researchers submitted a transmittal letter endorsed by the Dean of the College of Computer Studies to obtain authorization to conduct the study. In compliance with UCLM's research requirements, the researchers completed and secured the following supporting documents: Form 1S (Title Approval), the Proposal Approval Sheet signed by the Research Director, the payment receipt for the proposal defense (3C/3S), the Adviser's Acceptance (10S), the Statistician/Content Expert's Acceptance (11S), Form 2S (Compliance Checklist), the Grammarly Certificate (6S), and the attendance documentation of panel members (13S).  
&nbsp;Beyond institutional compliance, the researchers ensured that the development and implementation of Hiusa adhered to ethical practices throughout the research process. Before beginning the survey, the researchers gave each participant an informed consent statement outlining the study's goal, the voluntary nature of participation, and the participant's freedom to discontinue at any time without incurring any fees. The researchers handled organizational records obtained from Student Body Organizations, including financial documentation and event records, under strict confidentiality and used them solely to validate system requirements. The researchers did not disclose respondent identities or individual responses and presented only aggregated and anonymized data in the results. The researchers restricted access to system-generated data during development and testing to the research team. They did not share it with any third parties outside the scope of the study.

## **Software Engineering Methodology**

The researchers adopt the Agile development methodology, which emphasizes iterative and incremental development, continuous feedback, adaptability, and collaborative implementation throughout the development lifecycle (Ghimire & Charters, 2022). The researchers apply Agile to accommodate the integrated and multi-module scope of Hiusa, which includes AI-driven financial forecasting, budget advisory, workflow automation, event and attendance management, merchandise operations, and secure digital voting. This approach allows the researchers to develop, evaluate, and refine each module across successive sprints instead of delivering the system as a single monolithic release.

![][image8]

Figure 8: **Agile Methodology**

This chapter presents the development of Hiusa across three major phases. First, the Planning/Conception–Initiation Phase covers defining system requirements and preparing initial planning artifacts. Second, the Analysis–Design Phase focuses on system architecture design, AI component planning, and use case modeling. Finally, the Development/Construction/Build Phase covers the implementation, testing, deployment, and evaluation of each system module.  
&nbsp;The researchers selected Agile methodology to improve productivity, maintain development flexibility, and streamline both backend and frontend system implementation. This approach also enables the researchers to continuously develop, evaluate, and refine individual system components while identifying issues and opportunities for improvement throughout the development process. Given the integrated nature of Hiusa's functionalities, including AI-driven financial forecasting, budget advisory, workflow automation, event management, attendance monitoring, merchandise operations, and secure digital voting, Agile provides an effective environment for iterative enhancement and user-centered system development.

&nbsp;**Plan Phase**. The planning phase focused on identifying Hiusa's core objectives, determining SBO's operational requirements, and defining the functionalities needed to address the problems identified in Objective 1\. The researchers established the initial scope of the proposed system using data gathered from structured survey questionnaires and relevant organizational records. Based on the identified requirements, the researchers developed user stories that described user interaction across the system modules and used them to guide sprint planning throughout the development process.

&nbsp;**Design Phase**. During the design phase, the team produced wireframes and interface mockups for each module, covering key screens such as the financial dashboard, event management form, voting interface, merchandise catalog, and officer task board. During this phase, the researchers also designed the database schema and system architecture, including the AI component structure for financial forecasting and task delegation. Role-based access controls and security requirements were defined and incorporated into the design specifications before development began.

&nbsp;**Development Phase**. The researchers developed the system incrementally through multiple sprints, with each sprint focusing on implementing and refining a specific module. Development began with authentication and user management and progressively expanded to finance, elections, events, tasks, merchandise, and announcements. Developers aligned each sprint with the design specifications from the prior phase, and daily coordination ensured that new code met functional requirements and integrated correctly with completed modules.

&nbsp;**Testing Phase**. After each sprint, the researchers tested the newly developed features through unit testing, integration testing, and functional review. The researchers developed test cases based on the requirements defined during the design phase to verify that each module functioned as intended. The researchers corrected the issues identified during testing before closing the sprint and proceeding to develop the next module.

&nbsp;**Deployment Phase.** Once all modules were completed and verified, the system was deployed to a staging environment for evaluation by the research respondents. This process enabled continuous monitoring of actual system usage, identification of remaining issues, and verification that all features functioned correctly under actual operating conditions.

&nbsp;**Review Phase**. The review phase involved collecting evaluation data from the research respondents through the administered questionnaire and analyzing the results. The researchers gathered feedback from officers, the adviser, and students to identify necessary final adjustments and to determine the system's acceptability across all evaluation criteria.

## **Planning/Conception-Initiation Phase**

&nbsp;Following the Agile Methodology’s life cycle, in its related first phase, the planning or conception-initiation phase, the researchers began by establishing the foundations for developing Hiusa. Firstly, the researchers identified the organizational objectives, operational requirements, and existing challenges related to student governance, financial management, event coordination, merchandise operations, attendance monitoring, and election processes to define the scope and direction of the proposed system. Secondly, the researchers developed a detailed Program Workflow to visualize system processes and interactions and guide the integration of core functionalities in later development stages, including AI-driven financial forecasting, budget advisory, workflow automation, event planning assistance, and secure digital voting.

&nbsp;Moreover, to ensure the proposed approach remained aligned with organizational needs, requirements-gathering and validation activities were conducted to gain insights for refining system functionality and prioritizing essential features. As planning progressed, the researchers shifted to the technical preparation stage, creating a Functional Decomposition Diagram to break down Hiusa’s major system components, including financial management, event and activity management, merchandise operations, attendance tracking, digital voting, and AI-supported functionalities. Finally, the researchers prepared a detailed Gantt Chart to establish project schedules, key milestones, and development timelines, and to support systematic implementation and timely completion of the proposed system.

&nbsp;**Business Model Canvas.** The Business Model Canvas visually illustrates how Hiusa creates, delivers, and captures value within student governance and organizational management. It offers a thorough summary of the system's operational structure, highlighting its main advantages, potential areas for improvement, and opportunities to promote ongoing innovation and long-term sustainability.

![][image9]Figure 9: **Business Model Canvas of Hiusa**&nbsp;

The Business Model Canvas shown in the figure above depicts Hiusa's operational structure. It demonstrates how the platform creates, delivers, and captures value by integrating artificial intelligence and digital governance capabilities. It emphasizes the system's capability to streamline organizational operations, strengthen financial management, improve transparency, and support data-driven decision-making while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and sustainable organizational development.  
&nbsp;**Program Workflow.** The program workflow describes the general flow of user interaction within Hiusa, from initial access to task completion. Upon accessing the system, users enter their registered credentials on the login page to authenticate. The system verifies the user's identity and assigned role, then routes the authenticated user to a role-specific dashboard. From the dashboard, users navigate to the module relevant to their intended action. Officers with administrative privileges access management functions for finance, events, elections, merchandise, tasks, and announcements, while students access participation and monitoring interfaces based on their assigned permissions. Upon completing an action, the system confirms the transaction and updates the relevant records in the database.

Figure 10 presents the general program workflow of HIUSA, beginning when users access the web application and authenticate their accounts through proper credential validation. After the system verifies the submitted credentials, it identifies the user’s assigned role and redirects the user to the appropriate dashboard for the Admin, SBO Officer, Department Head, or Student. From the dashboard, users access only the modules and functions authorized for their role. If authentication fails, the system displays an error and allows the user to retry or recover the account before continuing.  
&nbsp;Administrators manage user accounts, announcements, elections, events, finances, merchandise, tasks, and automated workflows. They may create and update records, configure elections, manage event schedules, generate AI-assisted event plans, assign tasks, monitor budgets, produce reports, and process merchandise transactions. SBO officers perform operational activities such as drafting announcements, viewing assigned event responsibilities, updating task progress, monitoring financial records, assisting with attendance, and processing merchandise orders. Department heads focus on oversight and approval by reviewing events, budgets, elections, reports, and submitted requests, then approving or rejecting them with the appropriate remarks. The system records each decision and notifies the concerned users.  
&nbsp;Students use HIUSA to view announcements, events, activity schedules, and notifications. They may participate in authorized elections, record attendance, browse merchandise, submit orders and payments, track order status, receive claim tokens, and view digital receipts. Whenever a user completes an action, HIUSA validates the submitted information, updates the corresponding database records, and displays a confirmation, result, or status notification. The workflow then allows the user to perform another authorized activity or end the session, ensuring that all interactions remain organized, role-based, and properly recorded.

## **Analysis-Design Phase**

&nbsp;During the Agile development of Hiusa, the analysis-design phase of Hiusa’s Agile development turned system requirements into workable, user-centered designs. Wireframes, prototypes, use cases, and UI/UX layouts were produced by the team and refined in response to input. To facilitate a seamless transition to development, this phase established a clear design framework that combined usability, efficiency, and aesthetics.

&nbsp;**AI System Architecture.** The researchers embed Hiusa's AI components in two modules: Finance and Tasks. Both follow the same input–process–output structure: structured records already captured in the system database are transformed by a defined algorithm and returned to the interface as a decision-support output, not an autonomous or final action.

&nbsp;For financial forecasting, the system retrieves input from the transactions table, specifically the transaction\_date and type (income or expense), \`category\`, and \`amount\` fields recorded through the Finance module's digital ledger. These records are aggregated into a monthly time series for each category, forming the independent (time) and dependent (net amount) variables for an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression model. The model estimates coefficients that minimize the squared difference between actual and predicted monthly totals, producing a projected income and expense trend for the next 1 to 3 months. When a category's projected expense trend approaches or exceeds its remaining allocated balance in the \`budgets\` table, the system flags the category. It generates a real-time budget risk advisory for the assigned officer and the faculty adviser.

&nbsp;For task delegation, the system retrieves input from the tasks and users tables, specifically each officer's current open task count (status \= pending or in\_progress), role designation, and assignment history. A rule-based weighted scoring algorithm ranks eligible officers for a given task using three weighted factors: workload (fewer active tasks score higher, preventing overload on a small group of officers), role relevance (a role matching the task's category scores higher), and assignment recency (officers not recently assigned score higher, distributing delegation more evenly over time). The system returns the officer with the highest combined score as the top recommendation; the assigning officer retains final discretion to accept or override it, consistent with this study's position that AI outputs serve as decision support rather than autonomous decision-making.

**Use Case Diagrams.** A use case diagram presents a visual overview of how users interact with the system and identifies the system’s required functions based on user needs and activities. It is a component of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) used to document system users and their capabilities during system analysis. The four primary actors in Hiusa are Admin, SBO Officer, Department Head, and Student. The Admin actor has full access to all system functions, including user management, role assignment, audit log review, and system configuration. The SBO Officer actor manages the operational modules: finance, events, tasks, elections, merchandise, and announcements. The Department Head actor reviews and decides on approval requests for events, budget allocations, and elections to provide governance and oversight. The Student actor interacts with the system for participation-level functions: viewing announcements, voting in elections, placing merchandise orders, viewing assigned tasks, and registering for events.

**Storyboard.** The storyboard presents the initial interface designs for each module of the Hiusa system. The system designed each screen according to the authenticated user’s role and displayed only the functions and information relevant to the assigned access level. Key screens include the login page, the role-specific dashboard, the financial transactions list and forecast view, the event creation and management form, the election administration panel, the student voting interface, the merchandise catalog and order tracking screen, the task management board, and the announcements feed.  
**Module Name:** Authentication And User Management Module  
**Screen No**:1  
**Screen Name:** Login  
**Description:** This screen allows Admins, Advisers, Officers, and Students to securely access HIUSA using their registered School ID and Password. After successful authentication, the system redirects users to their assigned dashboard. Users who experience authentication issues may proceed to password recovery.

![][image45]  
Figure 43: **Login**

| ITEMS | TYPE | REQUIRED? | DATA TYPE | SAMPLE DATA |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| School ID | Input | Yes | String | 23104567 |
| Password | Input | Yes | Password | \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* |
| Show Password | Toggle | Optional | Boolean | true |
| Login Button | Button | Yes | Action | "Login" |
| Forgot Password Link | Link | Optional | Navigation | "Forgot Password?" |
| Validation Message | Text | Optional | String | "Invalid School ID or Password" |

**Logic**

1. The user enters their School ID and Password.  
2. The user may optionally select the Show Password toggle.  
3. The user clicks the "Login" button to proceed.  
   1. The system verifies that the user completes all required fields.&nbsp;  
   2. If required fields are incomplete, an error message is displayed.  
   3. If all fields are complete:

      The system verifies the entered credentials.

      1. If the credentials are invalid:  
         1. Displays the message: "Invalid School ID or Password."  
         2. Allows the user to retry login.  
      2. If the credentials are valid:  
         1. The system creates an authenticated session.  
         2. The system identifies the user's assigned role.  
         3. The system redirects the user to the corresponding dashboard.  
4. If the user clicks "Forgot Password?", they are redirected to the Forgot Password screen.

**Module Name:** Authentication And User Management Module  
**Screen No**: 2  
**Screen Name:** Forgot Password  
**Description:** This screen enables Admins, Advisers, Officers, and Students to initiate password recovery by entering their registered email address. Once submitted, the system sends a reset code to the provided email.

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;![][image46]Figure 44: **Forgot Password**

| Continue Button | Button | No | Action | “Continue” |
| Cancel Button | Button | No | Navigation | “Cancel” |

**Logic**

1\. The user enters their email address.

2\. The user clicks the “Continue” button.

2.1. The system checks if the email address exists in the database.

2.2. If the email does not exist, “Email is not yet registered.” is shown.

2.3. If the email exists, the user is redirected to the Code Verification screen.

3\. If the user clicks the “Cancel” button, they are redirected back to the Login screen.  
**Module Name:** Authentication And User Management Module  
**Screen No**: 3  
**Screen Name:** Code Verification  
**Description:** This screen allows Admins, Advisers, Officers, and Students to verify the reset code sent to their email. The user must enter the correct 6-digit code before proceeding to reset their password.

**![][image47]**  
Figure 45: **Code Verification**

| ITEMS | TYPE | REQUIRED? | DATA TYPE | SAMPLE DATA |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Verification Code | Input | Yes | Integer | 239125 |
| Verify Code | Button | Yes | Action | “Verify Code” |
| Resend Code | Button | Conditional | Action | “Resend Code” |
| Timer Indicator | Text | No | Timer | “5:00” |

**Logic**

1\. The email address supplied in the preceding step receives a 6-digit verification code from the system.

2\. The user enters the code into the input field.

3\. The user clicks the “Verify Code” button.

3.1. The system checks if the entered code matches the one sent.

3.2. If the code is incorrect, the system displays an error message: “Invalid code.”

3.3. If the code is correct, the user is redirected to the Reset Password screen.

4\. The user may click “Resend Code.”

4.1. The system checks the countdown timer.

4.2. If the timer reaches 0:00, the system sends a new code to the user’s email and resets the timer to 5:00.

4.3. If the timer has not expired, the “Resend Code” button remains disabled.

**Description:** This screen allows system admins to oversee, filter, and manage all registered user accounts within the portal. It features high-level summary cards displaying account statistics, multi-role filtering tabs, a search bar, and a comprehensive user directory table equipped with quick administrative action controls.&nbsp;

1\. The Admin navigates to the Manage User Accounts dashboard via the main sidebar menu.

2\. The system fetches and dynamically computes the real-time card metrics (Total Users, Officers, Students, Inactive).

3\. The Admin types a keyword into the "Search users..." input field.&nbsp;

3.1. The system filters the table records in real time, matching rows by User Name, Email, or Department.&nbsp;

3.2. If the system does not find a matching user record, it displays an empty state or the message: "No users found."

4\. The Admin clicks on a specific Role Filter Button ("Admin", "Adviser", "Officer", "Student").&nbsp;

4.1. The system updates the data view to display only the user accounts corresponding to the selected role.

5\. The Admin clicks on the "Register Account" tab next to Manage Accounts.&nbsp;

5.1. The system redirects the user to the manual account registration screen.

6\. The Admin clicks the Edit Icon next to a user profile row.&nbsp;

6.1. The system displays a modal or redirects the Admin to a form where they can modify the user's role, department, or profile permissions.

7\. The Admin clicks the Delete Icon next to a user profile row.

7.1. The system halts the action and displays a confirmation modal: "Are you sure you want to delete this user account?"&nbsp;

7.2. If the Admin confirms, the system updates the database, removes the user from the table, and recalculates the statistics banner metrics.

**Module Name:** Announcement Module  
**Screen No**: 10  
**Screen Name:** Manage Announcements  
**Description:** This screen allows users with administrative or officer privileges to oversee, track, and manage all organization announcements. It features a centralized data table displaying announcement titles, target audiences, operational categories, publication statuses, view metrics, and conditional action buttons to toggle publication states or remove listings.&nbsp;

![][image54]  
Figure 52: **Manage Announcements**

| ITEMS | TYPE | REQUIRED? | DATA TYPE | SAMPLE DATA |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Quick Search | Input | No | String | “Quick search” |
| Announcement Table | Component | Yes | Object Data | “General Assembly – Second Semester…” |
| Unpublish | Button | No | Action | “Unpublished” |
| Publish | Button | No | Action | “Publish” |
| Delete | Button | No | Action | “Trash Icon” |

**Logic**

1\. The user navigates to the Manage Announcements repository via the "Announcements \> Manage" option in the main navigation sidebar menu.

2\. The system pulls and displays all announcement records from the database in a chronological list.

3\. The system checks the publication state field for each unique announcement row.&nbsp;

3.1. If the status is "Published", the system displays a yellow Unpublish button and logs the total count under the "Views" metric column.&nbsp;

3.2. If the status is "Draft", the system displays a green Publish button and renders an empty dash indicator (—) under the "Views" metric column.

4\. The user clicks an active Unpublish button.&nbsp;

4.1. The system updates the announcement state to "Draft" in the database, replaces the toggle button with a green Publish button, and hides the announcement from the standard student dashboard stream.

5\. The user clicks an active Publish button.&nbsp;

5.1. The system transitions the announcement status state to "Published" in the database, replaces the toggle button with a yellow Unpublish button, and instantly makes the update visible to the specified target audience ("All Members" or "Officers").

6\. The user clicks the Delete Icon (red trash can) on any row item.&nbsp;

6.1. The system displays a confirmation prompt overlay: "Are you sure you want to delete this announcement?"&nbsp;

6.2. If confirmed by the user, the system updates the database parameters to purge the record and updates the table view.

4.2. Typing text into "Add custom position..." and clicking the Add button appends a brand-new custom rule option to the selection pool database.&nbsp;

6.1. Typing a keyword into the "Search student by name or ID..." text box narrows the directory roster down to matching string properties in real-time.&nbsp;

**Logic**

1\. The Student accesses the catalog by selecting the "Merchandise \> Order Merchandise" navigation menu link inside the sidebar navigation system.

2\. The system queries the inventory management database table to pull all active products, their current category types, unit prices, and remaining quantities.

3\. The system processes conditional evaluation rules based on remaining product quantities to set the appropriate Availability Status Badge:&nbsp;

3.1. If the stock volume exceeds defined safe thresholds, the system renders a green Available status badge.&nbsp;

3.2. If the stock volume falls below safety limits, the system renders a yellow Low Stock warning badge.

4\. For items mapped to size variations ("HIUSA Org Shirt – Navy"), the system displays the interactive Size Options Group row.&nbsp;

4.1. The student must select a specific size bubble item before the main reservation trigger becomes interactive.

5\. The student clicks the Reserve & Get Token button component.&nbsp;

5.1. The system creates a new transaction entry in the order tracking ledger with an initial state of "Pending", links it to the student's unique profile account ID, and generates a corresponding alphanumeric claim token.&nbsp;

5.2. The system subtracts the item quantity from the active store inventory count to flag those items as reserved and automatically redirects the student user to their personal "Claim Tokens" portal view.

**Module Name:** Merchandise Module  
**Screen No**: 34

**Description:** This screen allows student users to access a complete chronological log of their purchase history, including all merchandise reservations and acquisitions. It displays comprehensive tracking blocks representing separate order transactions, tracking status indicators, assigned claim token alphanumeric reference logs, payment confirmations, and fulfillment notes.&nbsp;

**Logic**

1\. The Student accesses their complete transaction receipt queue by selecting the "Merchandise \> My Orders" item inside the main navigation sidebar panel system.

2\. The system queries the transactional distribution database registry, retrieving all historical and active rows bound explicitly under the authenticated user's ID credentials, ordering records descending by date.

3\. The system processes and populates the Order Receipt Card array lists dynamically.

4\. The system evaluates current fulfillment indices to apply strict conditional formatting rules to individual card wrapper structures:&nbsp;

4.1. If an order's payment state is successfully authenticated but remains uncollected, the system displays a blue Paid badge component, shapes a blue outline layout boundary, and appends a green info icon caption stating: "Payment confirmed\! Show your token again to collect your Item."&nbsp;

4.2. If an administrator finalizes an over-the-counter stock handout, the system updates the badge component to a green Completed status tier, outlines the card container framework in green, and displays a celebration bag emoji footnote statement saying: "Item successfully claimed. Thank you\!"

5\. The student filters active history modules by typing target contextual phrases or specific item order descriptors into the global Quick Search entry box field to scale down the card array list view dynamically.

**Database Design**

HIUSA supports student governance and organizational management processes for student body organizations across the University of Cebu. It enables students, SBO officers, department heads, and administrators from different UC campuses and organizations to interact within one centralized system. The database organizes its schema into eight modules: Authentication and User Management; Dashboard; Announcements; Elections; Events and Attendance; Financial Management; Merchandise; and Task and Workflow Management. The users table centrally manages user profiles, system roles, account access, and SBO organizational positions. The database also supports AI-assisted functions, including OLS-based financial forecasting, Groq LLM-generated financial summaries and announcement drafts, AI-assisted event planning, Rule-Based Weighted Scoring for task delegation, and optional workflow automation. Foreign keys connect financial, event, election, merchandise, attendance, and task records to maintain data consistency. Shared tables for approvals, notifications, AI outputs, financial reports, and audit logs also support monitoring, reporting, transparency, and accountability across student organizations at the University of Cebu.

**Entity Relationship Diagram.** The Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) for HIUSA illustrates the core entities and relationships within the student governance and organizational management system. It organizes the database into eight modules: Authentication and User Management, Dashboard, Announcements, Elections, Events and Attendance, Financial Management, Merchandise, and Task and Workflow Management. The central entities include users, organizations, events, budgets, transactions, elections, merchandise, orders, tasks, and announcements, which define the system’s governance and operational structure. Event- and finance-related entities record budgets, transactions, attendance, financial forecasts, and generated reports, while election entities manage positions, party lists, candidates, votes, and election results. The ERD also represents AI-assisted components through entities that store event-planning outputs, financial summaries, announcement drafts, workflow results, and task-delegation explanations. Foreign-key relationships connect these entities to maintain data consistency and support role-based access, approval workflows, financial transparency, secure voting, merchandise fulfillment, task monitoring, workflow automation, and comprehensive reporting across student body organizations at the University of Cebu.

### **Data Dictionary**

A data dictionary functions as a tool to regulate access to and manipulation of a database. It comprises information on the database's format, contents, and structure, as well as the relationships among its elements.

Table 5  
DATA DICTIONARY OF USERS TABLE

| Field Name | Constraints | Data Type | Description |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| school\_id | PK, NOT NULL | int(10) | Primary identifier for the student, officer, adviser, or admin account.&nbsp; |
| organization\_id&nbsp; | FK NULL, INDEX | bigint(20) | References organizations(id).&nbsp; |
| first\_name | NOT NULL | varchar(60) | User's first name |
| last\_name | NOT NULL | varchar(60) | User's last name |
| is\_member | NOT NULL | tinyint(1)&nbsp; | Indicates if the user is a registered member |
| email | UNIQUE, NOT NULL | varchar(100) | User's email address |
| password\_hash | NOT NULL | varchar(255) | Encrypted password |
| role | NOT NULL | enum | User role (STUDENT, SBO\_OFFICER, ADMIN, DEPARTMENT\_HEAD) |
| biometric\_template | NULL | longblob | Fingerprint or biometric data for attendance |
| notification\_preferences | NULL | longtext | Stores the notification preferences value |
| created\_at | NULL | timestamp | The record creation time. |
| updated\_at | NULL | timestamp | The record's latest update time. |

&nbsp;

The USERS table serves as the primary repository for managing user accounts within the HIUSA platform. Its primary role is to securely store and manage essential information for students, officers, advisers, and administrators, including their personal details, organizational affiliation, membership status, authentication credentials, assigned system role, and biometric attendance information. The school\_id field serves as the table's primary key, uniquely identifying each user and establishing the relationships needed to connect the record to other governance-related modules within the database. In addition, the organization\_id field serves as a foreign key, linking each user to a specific student body organization and enabling organization-based data management and role assignment.

&nbsp;This table supports secure authentication and role-based access control through the email, password\_hash, and role attributes, ensuring that users are authenticated securely and granted access only to functionalities appropriate for their assigned roles as students, SBO officers, department heads, or administrators. The is\_member attribute identifies whether a user is an officially registered member of an organization, while the biometric\_template field securely stores fingerprint templates used by the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader for biometric attendance verification during organizational activities. Finally, the created\_at and updated\_at timestamp fields maintain a historical record of user account creation and subsequent profile modifications, supporting data integrity, administrative monitoring, and effective user management throughout the system.

It also incorporates AI-assisted task delegation via the is\_ai\_generated, ai\_recommendation\_note, role\_score, workload\_score, performance\_score, and final\_score fields, which store recommendations and weighted scores generated by the Rule-Based Decision-Making with Weighted Scoring algorithm. &nbsp;This table supports secure election management through the start\_time, end\_time, status, results\_visible, and approved\_at attributes, allowing the system to control election schedules, regulate voting periods, manage result visibility, and record approval before elections become active. The created\_at and updated\_at timestamp fields maintain a historical record of election creation and subsequent modifications, promoting transparency, accountability, and the integrity of the electronic voting process.

&nbsp;**Network Design.** HIUSA uses a secure, scalable, and web-based client-server architecture to support the operational and governance needs of Student Body Organizations at the University of Cebu–Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue. Client devices, including desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones, communicate with the centralized web application over the Internet, allowing students, officers, advisers, and administrators to access organizational services in real time. The application server processes user requests, executes core business logic through the Laravel backend, performs AI-assisted processing through integrated Python services and the Groq API, and stores organizational data using MySQL hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS). This architecture enables reliable management of financial records, organizational events, inventories, merchandise reservations, attendance logs, election records, workflow data, and user information while supporting scalable access across multiple student organizations.  
&nbsp;The network architecture also integrates the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader, which connects to an officer's workstation to perform real-time biometric attendance verification during organizational activities. The fingerprint scanner securely transmits the captured fingerprint data to the web application for authentication and attendance recording. In addition, the network supports AI-assisted services, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) financial forecasting, the Budget Advisory System, Rule-Based Weighted Scoring for officer task delegation, and a Large Language Model (LLM) accessed through the Groq API for announcement drafting, financial report summarization, AI-assisted event planning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Through this integrated network infrastructure, HIUSA enables secure electronic voting, financial management, inventory monitoring, workflow automation, event coordination, and real-time organizational monitoring, providing student body organizations with a centralized, reliable, and intelligent governance platform.

**![][image88]**  
Figure 86: **Network Design**

The network design of HIUSA illustrates how client devices and integrated hardware communicate with the centralized web application to support real-time student governance operations. During organizational activities, the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader captures biometric attendance data through an officer's workstation and securely transmits it to the web server over the Internet for authentication and attendance recording. The server also processes organizational transactions, event information, inventory records, election activities, and workflow data while executing AI-assisted functionalities, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression for financial forecasting, the Budget Advisory System for spending recommendations, and the Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm for officer task delegation. Additionally, a Large Language Model (LLM) accessed via the Groq API generates AI-assisted announcements, financial report summaries, event-planning recommendations, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) explanations. The processed information is then delivered to the web dashboards of students, officers, advisers, and administrators, enabling secure, real-time access to financial records, organizational events, inventory information, election results, attendance records, workflow updates, and AI-assisted decision-support tools.&nbsp;&nbsp;  
&nbsp;**Network Model.** HIUSA uses a centralized web-based architecture that integrates a secure application server with a centralized database to support student governance operations at the University of Cebu–Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue. The application server manages user authentication, organizational transactions, financial management, event coordination, inventory monitoring, electronic voting, workflow automation, and communication between client devices and the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader, which performs biometric attendance verification. The centralized database securely stores user information, financial records, inventory data, attendance logs, election records, event information, merchandise reservations, organizational documents, and other operational data required by the system. In addition, the server executes AI-assisted functionalities, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression for financial forecasting, the Budget Advisory System, the Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm for officer task delegation, and a Large Language Model (LLM) accessed through the Groq API for announcement drafting, financial report summarization, AI-assisted event planning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI).  
&nbsp;To protect organizational and user data, HIUSA implements secure user authentication, encrypted password storage, role-based access control, and secure communication between client devices, biometric hardware, and the web application. These security mechanisms ensure that system functionalities and organizational information are accessible only to authorized users according to their assigned roles as students, officers, advisers, or administrators, thereby promoting data integrity, confidentiality, and secure organizational management.

&nbsp;**Network Topology.** The network topology of HIUSA follows a star topology, in which students, officers, advisers, and administrators connect directly to a centralized web server through the Internet using their web browsers. This architecture supports secure, centralized communication between client devices and the server, enabling users to access organizational services such as financial management, event coordination, inventory monitoring, electronic voting, merchandise reservation, attendance monitoring, workflow management, and organizational reporting from multiple devices.  
&nbsp;This centralized configuration facilitates efficient communication between client devices, the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader, and the application server, allowing real-time processing of organizational data and biometric attendance records. It also supports the execution of AI-assisted functionalities, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression for financial forecasting, the Budget Advisory System, the Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm for officer task delegation, and a Large Language Model (LLM) accessed through the Groq API for announcement drafting, financial report summarization, AI-assisted event planning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). By centralizing communication and data processing, the network topology promotes secure system access, reliable data management, and scalable support for the operational needs of student body organizations at the University of Cebu Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue.

## **Development/Construction/Build Phase**

During this phase, developers and system analysts develop a clear understanding of the application software, enabling them to effectively construct, implement, and maintain the system after installation.  
&nbsp;**Technology Stack Diagram.** The Technology Stack Diagram illustrates the collection of technologies, frameworks, platforms, and hardware components utilized in the development and operation of HIUSA. The system architecture integrates four primary components: Frontend, Backend, Database, and Biometric Integration. Each component performs a distinct function in delivering the system's overall functionality.  
&nbsp;The development team uses React for the Frontend and utilizes Vite as the build tool to support rapid development and optimize system performance. The user interface uses Tailwind CSS, which provides responsive, consistent designs across devices and screen sizes. Together, these technologies ensure a modern, intuitive, and user-friendly experience for students, officers, advisers, and administrators.  
&nbsp;The Backend utilizes Laravel, a robust PHP framework that manages the system's Application Programming Interface (API), business logic layer, user authentication, secure routing, data processing, workflow automation, and core organizational operations, including event management, inventory monitoring, financial management, merchandise pre-ordering, and electronic voting. In addition, the Backend integrates a Python-based API that handles HIUSA's AI-assisted functionalities. The Python API executes the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression model for financial forecasting, the Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm for officer task delegation, and facilitates communication with the Groq API to access the Large Language Model (LLM) for announcement drafting, financial report summarization, AI-assisted event planning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Together, Laravel and the Python API provide a scalable backend architecture that supports both organizational management and AI-assisted decision support.&nbsp;  
&nbsp;The Database layer utilizes MySQL hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to provide secure, scalable, and structured data storage. It manages organizational information, including user accounts, announcements, events, budgets, inventory records, merchandise orders, attendance logs, and voting data while ensuring data integrity, reliability, and accessibility.  
&nbsp;To support biometric attendance verification, the system incorporates a Biometric Integration Layer that enables communication between the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader and the Laravel backend through the device's vendor-provided Software Development Kit (SDK). This integration captures and verifies fingerprint data during organizational activities, allowing the system to authenticate user identities and automatically record attendance in real time. Biometric templates and attendance records are securely processed and stored within the system, improving attendance accuracy, reducing manual verification, and strengthening accountability throughout organizational events.&nbsp;

![][image91]

Figure 89: **Technology Stack Diagram**

The developers use Vite, React.js, and Tailwind CSS to develop the system's frontend, providing a fast, responsive, and user-friendly web interface for students, officers, advisers, and administrators. Core business logic, user authentication, financial transactions, event management, inventory control, workflow automation, and organizational operations are all managed by the Laravel and PHP-built backend. Hiusa leverages Python to implement its AI-based features, enabling the system to perform financial forecasting using the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression and to recommend officer task assignments through a Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm. Data is stored using MySQL and hosted through Amazon Web Services (AWS) to provide reliable, scalable, and secure data management for financial records, inventory information, event data, attendance logs, merchandise orders, election records, and organizational documents. For AI-assisted text generation, the system integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) through the Groq API to support announcement drafting, financial report summarization, AI-assisted event planning, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). Furthermore, HIUSA integrates the DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader to provide secure biometric attendance verification during organizational activities, ensuring accurate and efficient attendance monitoring.&nbsp;

**Program Specification.** The program specification defines the essential processes, data input requirements, and expected functionalities that the HIUSA System must perform. It outlines the system's objectives and the tasks it must execute to optimize student organization management.&nbsp;

**Functional Requirements.**&nbsp;

&nbsp;The system must provide the following functionalities:

1. **Authentication Process** – the system will verify the identity of the user (Student, SBO Officer,  Admin, or Department Head) attempting to access the HIUSA platform securely.  
2. **Login & Registration Process** – the system allows users to securely log in or register their accounts using their school credentials and personal information.  
3. **Announcements & Notifications** – the system enables officers and admins to publish announcements and dispatch real-time notifications to users.  
4. **Events & Attendance Management** – the system allows officers to create events, and users to check in using biometrics or manually, capturing accurate attendance records.  
5. **Task Management** – the system tracks event-related tasks, assignees, and deadlines, and features an AI recommendation note for improved task allocation.  
6. **Financial Management** – the system manages event budgets, records transactions (income/expenses), and features financial forecasts predicting future income and expenses.  
7. **Merchandise & Order Management** – the system enables students to browse merchandise, place orders, and receive a reference token. Officers can process and approve these orders for claiming.  
8. **Elections & Voting Management** – the system facilitates transparent elections by managing party lists, candidates, and election positions.  
9. **User Management** – the system enables administrators to view and manage all student, SBO officer, and department head accounts.

**Nonfunctional Requirements.**  
&nbsp;The following are the nonfunctional requirements of the system:

1. The system maintains continuous availability and minimizes operational downtime.&nbsp;  
2. A stable and active Internet connection supports real-time updates and synchronization.&nbsp;&nbsp;  
3. The web application must run smoothly on modern web browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari).&nbsp;  
4. Users must input accurate and complete information during registration and operations.&nbsp;  
5. Only authenticated and authorized users may access specific role-based features and data.&nbsp;  
6. The web application must provide a responsive user interface that automatically adjusts to varying screen sizes and resolutions, ensuring usability and consistent performance across desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices.&nbsp;

**Human Resources Specifications.**  
&nbsp;The Hiusa system supports the following user groups:

1. Students  
2. SBO Officers  
3. Administrators  
4. Department Heads

**APPENDIX C**  
**SURVEY QUESTIONNAIRE**

Dear Participants,

We respectfully invite you to participate in this survey aimed to gather valuable insights regarding your experiences with and assessment of the proposed AI-integrated student governance and financial management system. The proposed system is designed to improve the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of **Student Body Organizations (SBOs)** at the University of Cebu – Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue through AI-assisted financial management, centralized event and task coordination, digital elections, attendance monitoring, announcement dissemination, and automated reporting.

Your responses will help us evaluate the system's functionality, usability, reliability, and overall acceptability among students, Student Body Organization officers, advisers, and department heads. The survey will only take approximately 5 to 10 minutes to complete.

&nbsp;

Your Participation Matters:

* **Confidentiality and Anonymity**: All responses will be strictly confidential and anonymous. No personal names or identifying information will be used in our analysis.  
* **Data Security**: Only the research team will have access to the collected data. Your privacy is our top priority.  
* **Academic Purpose**: The data gathered will be used strictly for academic research and presented only in an aggregated or summarized form.

Your input is vital to the development, validation, and continuous improvement of Hiusa and will contribute significantly to building a more efficient, transparent, and AI-assisted student governance and financial management system for Student Body Organizations.

&nbsp;

Thank you for your time, cooperation, and support\!

Warm regards,  
**The Research Team**  
Borgueta, John Carlo L.  
Cavan, Ayn Lorebelle E.  
Ompad, Mary Jasmin P.  
Ventic, Jade Mykel R.

**Section C: Mechanism or Techniques of the ProposedSystem**

Direction: Kindly indicate your response by placing a slash (/) in the appropriate column that best reflects your perception of each statement using the following scale.&nbsp;

| STRONGLY AGREE (5) | AGREE (4) | NEUTRAL(3) | DISAGREE (2) | STRONGLY DISAGREE (1) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **SA** | **A** | **N** | **D** | **SD** |

&nbsp;

| &nbsp;Mechanism or Techniques of the Proposed System | &nbsp;SA | A | N | D | SD |
| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| The system should analyze historical financial transactions to estimate future organizational income and expenses. *(Ordinary Least Squares Linear Regression – financial forecasting)*&nbsp; | &nbsp; |  |  |  |  |
| The system should use financial forecasts and existing budget records to identify possible overspending. *(Budget Advisory System – rule-based financial recommendations)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should present financial forecasts and budget recommendations in a clear and understandable format. *(Groq Large Language Model and Explainable AI – financial explanation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate suggested timelines, resource requirements, and preparation checklists based on event details. *(Groq Large Language Model – AI-assisted event planning)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should verify student attendance through fingerprint identification during organizational activities. *(Biometric identification – DigitalPersona 4500\)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should recommend suitable officers for tasks based on their assigned roles, current workload, and previous performance. *(Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm – task delegation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate an organized sequence of tasks and deadlines for each event or activity. *(Workflow Automation – task and process generation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should prevent an eligible student from submitting more than one vote during an election. *(One-student-one-vote validation – duplicate-vote prevention)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should automatically count valid votes after the election period. *(Automated vote tallying – election result generation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| A unique claim token will create a verifiable record for each merchandise release. (Tokenized Queue System – claim verification)&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| Automatic inventory updates will improve the accuracy of recorded stock levels. (Dynamic Inventory Tracking – real-time stock monitoring)&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |

**Section C: Mechanism or Techniques of the proposed system**

Direction: Kindly indicate your response by placing a slash (/) in the appropriate column that best reflects your perception of each statement using the following scale.&nbsp;

| STRONGLY AGREE (5) | AGREE (4) | NEUTRAL(3) | DISAGREE (2) | STRONGLY DISAGREE (1) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **SA** | **A** | **N** | **D** | **SD** |

&nbsp;

| &nbsp;Mechanism or Techniques of the Proposed System | &nbsp;SA | A | N | D | SD |
| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| The system should use historical transaction data and current budget records to generate responsible spending recommendations. *(Ordinary Least Squares Linear Regression and Budget Advisory System – financial forecasting and decision support)*&nbsp; | &nbsp; |  |  |  |  |
| The system should explain financial forecasts and budget recommendations in a clear and understandable format. *(Groq Large Language Model and Explainable AI – interpretation of financial insights)*&nbsp;&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate suggested timelines, resource needs, and preparation checklists based on the details of an event. *(Groq Large Language Model – AI-assisted Event Planning Assistant)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should use fingerprint verification to record student attendance during organizational activities. *(Biometric Identification – DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should recommend suitable officers for tasks based on their roles, current workloads, and previous performance. *(Rule-Based Weighted Scoring Algorithm – AI-assisted task delegation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate an organized sequence of tasks and deadlines for each event or organizational activity. *(Workflow Automation – task and process generation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should allow each authenticated and eligible student to submit only one vote during an election. *(User authentication and one-student-one-vote validation – duplicate-vote prevention)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should automatically count valid votes after the approved election period ends. *Automated Vote Tallying – election result generation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate a unique claim token for each approved merchandise reservation. *(Tokenized Queue System – merchandise claim verification)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should automatically update stock records when merchandise is reserved, cancelled, or released. *(Dynamic Inventory Tracking – real-time stock monitoring)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should assist officers in preparing clear and organized announcement drafts. *(Groq Large Language Model – AI-assisted announcement drafting)*&nbsp;&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should require authorized review before an official announcement is published. *(Announcement Approval Workflow – content review and authorization)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |

**Section C: Mechanism or Techniques of the proposed system**

Direction: Kindly indicate your response by placing a slash (/) in the appropriate column that best reflects your perception of each statement using the following scale.&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| STRONGLY AGREE (5) | AGREE (4) | NEUTRAL(3) | DISAGREE (2) | STRONGLY DISAGREE (1) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **SA** | **A** | **N** | **D** | **SD** |

&nbsp;

| &nbsp;Mechanism or Techniques of the Proposed System | &nbsp;SA | A | N | D | SD |
| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| The system should organize approved Student Body Organization events in one activity calendar. *(Centralized Activity Calendar – event information access)*&nbsp; | &nbsp; |  |  |  |  |
| The system should notify students about new events and approaching schedules. *(Automated Notification System – timely event updates)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should use fingerprint verification to record student attendance during organizational activities. *(Biometric Identification – DigitalPersona 4500 Fingerprint Reader)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should require students to sign in before accessing an active election. *(User Authentication – controlled election access)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should allow each eligible student to submit only one vote during an election. *(One-Student-One-Vote Validation – duplicate-vote prevention)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should automatically count valid votes after the election period ends. *(Automated Vote Tallying – election result generation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should display the current availability of merchandise before a student places an order. *(Dynamic Inventory Tracking – real-time stock information)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should allow students to reserve available merchandise online. *(Online Pre-Ordering System – digital merchandise reservation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should allow students to submit proof of GCash payment for officer verification. *(Digital Payment Verification – payment confirmation)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should generate a unique claim token for each approved merchandise order. *(Tokenized Queue System – merchandise claim verification)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should automatically update the status of each merchandise order. *(Order Status Tracking – pending, paid, and completed records)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should display published announcements in one searchable location. *(Centralized Announcement Feed – organized information access)*&nbsp; |  |  |  |  |  |
| The system should limit student access to functions and information intended for the Student role.*(Role-Based Access Control – controlled system access)* |  |  |  |  |  |
